Two seconds is the editor process cleanup grace period between terminate and kill, followed by awaiting process exit. It neither limits a model/Tool run nor abandons cleanup. Existing editor argv/error/file-cleanup tests are referenced; no direct exhaustive forced-kill timing test is claimed.

Two workers is the local bounded background image-rendering pool owned by ImageRenderer. It does not authorize network/file Tool effects or configure model concurrency. Existing path/artifact validation, pixel bounds, generation invalidation and close behavior remain intact.

Ten seconds controls when the restart UI displays a waiting notice. Shielded cleanup is still awaited after the notice, so it is not an execution deadline or permission to restart before cleanup. Existing actual restart/command cleanup tests do not claim exhaustive notice-timer coverage.

Eight is the local completion popup maximum visible height, not a data retention bound or execution policy. PTK keeps the completion collection and scroll state; this occurrence only sizes its viewport.

The 0.02-second values are Hub-owned PTK key-sequence decoding latency while the view is active. The original host values are restored on minimize/close. Escape/Alt navigation neither grants execution nor interrupts a Run implicitly.

This is the exact-type/version rejection in the model-value reader, parameterized by the actual ModelMessage, ModelRequest or ModelResponse owner. All three declare their own integer VERSION; no imported/global version, old-format branch or inferred value is used. The same helper then requires every current dataclass field, and nested readers independently require all fields including nullable evidence. The AST local-class heuristic cannot prove this explicit helper call relation. Bool, float, text, missing, unsupported versions and missing/extra nested fields are tested without mutating source records. This review covers only these precise checks, not other version readers.
